- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests.** Create `server/test/ccd-docs-fetch.test.ts`:

````ts
// `docs-fetch` (docs reader spec 2026-10-01 §2 (g); §2 rows 41, 42, 43 and 59, and the ccd halves of rows 61
// and 62). End to end through the shipped dispatcher (`runCcdDocs`) wherever a fixture HOME can build the
// condition, and as helper units (`unitJson`, which imports `_docs_py` out of `ccd/ccd` as a module) where it
// cannot: a fetch that outlives a lowered bound, a lock that vanishes before its lstat, a canned stderr, and the
// pure classifier. Fixture refs move only through `h.git` (the real binary with the fixture identity, never the
// PATH recorder), and every origin change is made inside the bare origin itself, so nothing but the verb under
// test touches the main checkout's refs, its FETCH_HEAD or its hooks.
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { harnessBin, makeCcdHarness, type CcdHarness } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { parseOneLine, plantGitRecorder, REAL_GIT, runCcdDocs, type RecordedGitCall } from './ccdDocsHelpers.js';
import { unitJson } from './docsHelperPy.js';

type Answer = Record<string, unknown>;
type Stamp = {
  v: number; branch: string; attemptMs: number; lastOutcome: string; okMs: number | null; okCommit: string | null;
};

let h: CcdHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makeCcdHarness('ccd-docs-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

const originOf = (name: string): string => path.join(h.home, 'origins', `${name}.git`);
const rev = (dir: string, ref: string): string => h.git(dir, 'rev-parse', ref);
/** The full refnames `for-each-ref` lists under `pattern` in `dir`. */
const refsUnder = (dir: string, pattern: string): string[] =>
  h.git(dir, 'for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname)', pattern).split('\n').filter((l) => l !== '');

let advanceSeq = 0;
/** A new commit on the bare origin's `branch`, by `commit-tree` and `update-ref` in the origin itself, so the main
 *  checkout learns of it only through a fetch. The counter keeps two advances in one second distinct: identical
 *  tree, parent and message would be the same commit. */
const advanceOrigin = (name: string, branch = 'main'): string => {
  advanceSeq += 1;
  const o = originOf(name);
  const c = h.git(o, 'commit-tree', `refs/heads/${branch}^{tree}`, '-p', `refs/heads/${branch}`, '-m', `advance ${advanceSeq}`);
  h.git(o, 'update-ref', `refs/heads/${branch}`, c);
  return c;
};

/** §2 (g) step 6's line, transcribed token for token from the spec: the argv after `git` that the recorder logs. */
const SPEC_FETCH_LINE = (main: string, b: string): string[] => [
  '--no-pager', '-c', 'core.hooksPath=/dev/null', '-c', 'core.fsmonitor=false', '-c', 'gc.auto=0',
  '-c', 'maintenance.auto=false', '-c', 'fetch.writeCommitGraph=false', '-c', 'submodule.recurse=false',
  '-c', 'fetch.recurseSubmodules=false', '-c', 'fetch.fsckObjects=true', '-c', 'transfer.fsckObjects=true',
  '-C', main,
  'fetch', '--quiet', '--no-tags', '--no-prune', '--no-recurse-submodules', '--no-write-fetch-head',
  '--no-auto-gc', '--no-auto-maintenance', '--no-show-forced-updates',
  '--end-of-options', 'origin', `+refs/heads/${b}:refs/remotes/origin/${b}`,
];

/** The recorded calls whose subcommand (the token after `-C <dir>`) is `fetch`. */
const fetchCalls = (calls: RecordedGitCall[]): RecordedGitCall[] =>
  calls.filter((c) => { const i = c.argv.indexOf('-C'); return i >= 0 && c.argv[i + 2] === 'fetch'; });

/** `ccd docs-fetch --project <project> [--branch <branch>]` through the dispatcher, as its one parsed line. */
const fetchDocs = (project: string, branch: string | null = null, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {}): Answer =>
  parseOneLine(runCcdDocs(h, ['docs-fetch', '--project', project, ...(branch === null ? [] : ['--branch', branch])], env));

const sha256 = (s: string): string => createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex');
/** Where §2 (g) step 4 keeps a stamp, derived here independently of the helper: `$REG/docs/fetch/<32 hex of
 *  sha256(realpath(common dir))>/<32 hex of sha256(branch)>.json`. */
const stampFile = (main: string, branch: string): string => path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', 'docs', 'fetch',
  sha256(fs.realpathSync(path.join(main, '.git'))).slice(0, 32), `${sha256(branch).slice(0, 32)}.json`);
const readStampFile = (p: string): Stamp => JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8')) as Stamp;
/** Moves a stamp's attempt `ms` into the past: the floor's only input, so this stands in for waiting. */
const ageStamp = (p: string, ms: number): void => {
  const s = readStampFile(p);
  fs.writeFileSync(p, JSON.stringify({ ...s, attemptMs: s.attemptMs - ms }));
};

/** Python that answers `docs-fetch --project <project>` through the helper's own `run` (the envelope and the
 *  failure body included) and prints that line parsed. `pre` runs first, after `H` is loaded: a `Sys` swap, or
 *  a `VERBS` entry that lowers a bound by passing it. */
const fetchUnit = (project: string, pre: string[] = []): string => [
  'import json',
  'import os',
  ...pre,
  "HOME = os.environ['HOME']",
  "argv = ['docs-fetch', os.path.join(HOME, 'projects'), os.path.join(HOME, 'worktrees'),",
  `        os.path.join(HOME, '.cc-sessions'), '--project', ${JSON.stringify(project)}]`,
  "out(json.loads(H.run(argv).decode('utf-8')))",
].join('\n');

/** A `Sys` whose `spawn` answers the fetch itself with `rc` and `stderr`, and runs every other git call for real. */
const cannedFetch = (rc: number, stderr: string): string[] => [
  'class CannedFetch(H.Sys):',
  '    def spawn(self, argv, *a, **k):',
  "        i = argv.index('-C') if '-C' in argv else -1",
  "        if i >= 0 and argv[i + 2:i + 3] == ['fetch']:",
  `            return H.Spawned(rc=${rc}, out=b'', err=${JSON.stringify(stderr)}.encode('utf-8'), timed_out=False, overflow=False)`,
  '        return H.Sys.spawn(self, argv, *a, **k)',
  'H.SYS = CannedFetch()',
];

/** A `Sys` whose `lstat` of any `*.lock` path fails with `errnoName`, and stats everything else for real. */
const lockLstatFails = (errnoName: 'ENOENT' | 'EACCES'): string[] => [
  'import errno',
  'class LockLstat(H.Sys):',
  '    def lstat(self, path, *a, **k):',
  "        if str(path).endswith('.lock'):",
  `            raise OSError(errno.${errnoName}, 'planted by the unit', path)`,
  '        return H.Sys.lstat(self, path, *a, **k)',
  'H.SYS = LockLstat()',
];

const sleep = (ms: number): Promise<void> => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
const alive = (pid: number): boolean => {
  try { process.kill(pid, 0); return true; } catch { return false; }
};

describe('docs-fetch hygiene: the exact line, and nothing but one ref moves (rows 41 and 16, R7)', () => {
  it('records step 6 byte for byte, leaves FETCH_HEAD, tags, other branches, local refs and hooks alone (ctl: a plain fetch)', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    const o = originOf('demo');
    const old = rev(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/main');
    const next = advanceOrigin('demo');
    h.git(o, 'update-ref', 'refs/tags/v1', next);
    h.git(o, 'update-ref', 'refs/heads/ws/x', next);
    h.git(main, 'branch', 'ws/x', old);
    const fetchHead = path.join(main, '.git', 'FETCH_HEAD');
    fs.writeFileSync(fetchHead, 'sentinel: no fetch may rewrite this\n');
    const pinned = new Date('2001-02-03T04:05:06Z');
    fs.utimesSync(fetchHead, pinned, pinned);
    const marker = path.join(h.home, 'reference-transaction-fired');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(main, '.git', 'hooks'), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, '.git', 'hooks', 'reference-transaction'),
      `#!/bin/sh\necho fired >> '${marker}'\n`, { mode: 0o755 });
    const rec = plantGitRecorder(h.home);

    const a = fetchDocs('demo', null, { GIT_SSH_COMMAND: 'ssh -o BatchMode=yes', GIT_DIR: path.join(h.home, 'decoy.git') });
    expect(a).toMatchObject({
      v: 1, verb: 'docs-fetch', ok: true, branch: 'main', trackedRef: 'refs/remotes/origin/main',
      defaultVia: 'default:origin-head', before: old, after: next, moved: 'updated', stamp: 'written',
    });
    const fetches = fetchCalls(rec.calls());
    expect(fetches.map((c) => c.argv)).toEqual([SPEC_FETCH_LINE(path.join(h.home, 'projects', 'demo'), 'main')]);
    // The fetch environment: the read runner's scrub and pins, plus the transport keep-list (§2 (a)).
    expect(fetches[0]!.env).toMatchObject({ LC_ALL: 'C', GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0', GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH: '1',
      GIT_SSH_COMMAND: 'ssh -o BatchMode=yes' });
    expect(fetches[0]!.env).not.toHaveProperty('GIT_DIR');
    expect(rev(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/main')).toBe(next);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(fetchHead, 'utf8')).toBe('sentinel: no fetch may rewrite this\n');
    expect(fs.statSync(fetchHead).mtimeMs).toBe(pinned.getTime());
    expect(refsUnder(main, 'refs/tags')).toEqual([]);
    expect(refsUnder(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/ws')).toEqual([]);
    expect(rev(main, 'refs/heads/ws/x')).toBe(old);
    expect(fs.existsSync(marker), 'core.hooksPath=/dev/null kept the reference-transaction hook from firing').toBe(false);

    // CONTROL (security M1): a plain fetch of the same origin fires the hook, follows the tag, takes the second
    // branch and rewrites FETCH_HEAD, so each absence above was the line's doing, not the fixture's.
    advanceOrigin('demo');
    h.git(main, 'fetch', '-q', 'origin');
    expect(fs.existsSync(marker)).toBe(true);
    expect(refsUnder(main, 'refs/tags')).toEqual(['refs/tags/v1']);
    expect(refsUnder(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/ws')).toEqual(['refs/remotes/origin/ws/x']);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(fetchHead, 'utf8')).not.toBe('sentinel: no fetch may rewrite this\n');
  });

  it('defaultVia is present iff --branch is absent, and moved tells created, updated and unchanged apart', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    const tip = rev(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/main');
    const a = fetchDocs('demo', 'main');
    expect(a).toMatchObject({ ok: true, branch: 'main', before: tip, after: tip, moved: 'unchanged', stamp: 'written' });
    expect(a).not.toHaveProperty('defaultVia');
    h.git(main, 'update-ref', '-d', 'refs/remotes/origin/main');
    ageStamp(stampFile(main, 'main'), 60_000);
    expect(fetchDocs('demo', 'main')).toMatchObject({ ok: true, before: null, after: tip, moved: 'created' });
    ageStamp(stampFile(main, 'main'), 60_000);
    const next = advanceOrigin('demo');
    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: true, defaultVia: 'default:origin-head', before: tip, after: next, moved: 'updated' });
  });
});

describe('docs-fetch refusals before any fetch (steps 1-3)', () => {
  it('no remote.origin.url answers remote-absent, and nothing is fetched or stamped', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');

    expect(fetchCalls(rec.calls())).toEqual([]);

  });

      { env: { ...process.env, HOME: h.home }, stdio: 'ignore' });

      'import json',
      `cases = json.loads(${JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(CASES))})`,
      'out([H.classify_fetch(rc, err, to) for _name, rc, err, to, _want in cases])',
    ].join('\n'));
    expect(CASES.map((c, i) => [c[0], got[i]])).toEqual(CASES.map((c) => [c[0], c[4]]));
  });

  it('a fetch that outlives a lowered bound answers fetch-timeout, and its grandchild is gone (killpg)', async () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    const pidFile = path.join(h.home, 'fetch-grandchild.pid');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(harnessBin(h.home), 'git'), [
      '#!/bin/sh',
      '# A git whose fetch never finishes: it backgrounds a sleeping grandchild, records its pid, and waits on it.',
      'case " $* " in',
      `  *' fetch --quiet '*) sleep 30 & echo "$!" > '${pidFile}'; wait; exit 0 ;;`,
      'esac',
      `exec '${REAL_GIT}' "$@"`,
      '',
    ].join('\n'), { mode: 0o755 });
    const a = unitJson<Answer>(h.home, fetchUnit('demo', [
      "H.VERBS['docs-fetch'] = lambda ctx, a: H.verb_fetch(ctx, a, fetch_s=1)",
    ]), { timeoutMs: 30_000 });
    expect(a).toMatchObject({ ok: false, failure: 'fetch-timeout', branch: 'main' });
    expect(a['elapsedMs'] as number, 'the lowered 1 s bound fired, not the 40 s one').toBeLessThan(10_000);
    const pid = Number(fs.readFileSync(pidFile, 'utf8').trim());
    expect(pid).toBeGreaterThan(1);
    for (let i = 0; i < 80 && alive(pid); i++) await sleep(50);
    expect(alive(pid), `grandchild ${pid} outlived the fetch`).toBe(false);
    expect(readStampFile(stampFile(main, 'main')), 'a timed-out attempt is still an attempt').toMatchObject({
      v: 1, branch: 'main', lastOutcome: 'fetch-timeout', okMs: null, okCommit: null });
  });
});

describe('docs-fetch ref-locked and its lock age (rows 42 and 61, ccd half)', () => {
  const lockedFetch = (ageMs: number): { a: Answer; spanMs: number } => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    advanceOrigin('demo');
    const lock = path.join(main, '.git', 'refs', 'remotes', 'origin', 'main.lock');
    fs.writeFileSync(lock, '');
    const t0 = Date.now();
    const then = new Date(t0 - ageMs);
    fs.utimesSync(lock, then, then);
    const a = fetchDocs('demo');
    return { a, spanMs: Date.now() - t0 };
  };

  it('a lock touched 5 s ago answers ref-locked with lockAgeMs about 5000', () => {
    const { a, spanMs } = lockedFetch(5_000);
    expect(a).toMatchObject({ ok: false, failure: 'ref-locked', branch: 'main' });
    expect(String(a['detail'])).toContain('cannot lock ref');
    // The true age lies between 5000 and 5000 plus the run's own length; 10 ms covers clock rounding.
    expect(a['lockAgeMs'] as number).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(5_000 - 10);
    expect(a['lockAgeMs'] as number).toBeLessThanOrEqual(5_000 + spanMs + 10);
  });

  it('a 120 s old lock answers lockAgeMs about 120000', () => {
    const { a, spanMs } = lockedFetch(120_000);
    expect(a).toMatchObject({ ok: false, failure: 'ref-locked' });
    expect(a['lockAgeMs'] as number).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(120_000 - 10);
    expect(a['lockAgeMs'] as number).toBeLessThanOrEqual(120_000 + spanMs + 10);
  });

  it('a lock gone before its lstat answers lockAgeMs null; an lstat that fails otherwise leaves the field out', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    advanceOrigin('demo');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, '.git', 'refs', 'remotes', 'origin', 'main.lock'), '');
    const gone = unitJson<Answer>(h.home, fetchUnit('demo', lockLstatFails('ENOENT')));
    expect(gone).toMatchObject({ ok: false, failure: 'ref-locked', lockAgeMs: null });
    ageStamp(stampFile(main, 'main'), 60_000);
    const unseen = unitJson<Answer>(h.home, fetchUnit('demo', lockLstatFails('EACCES')));
    expect(unseen).toMatchObject({ ok: false, failure: 'ref-locked' });
    expect(unseen, '"could not look" is not "gone"').not.toHaveProperty('lockAgeMs');
  });
});

describe('docs-fetch fsck (row 59, R16)', () => {
  it('an origin holding a malformed tree answers fetch-rejected-objects and the ref does not move (ctl: no fsck flags)', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    const o = originOf('demo');
    const blob = Buffer.from(h.git(o, 'rev-parse', 'refs/heads/main:README.md'), 'hex');
    const entry = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('100644 a\0', 'latin1'), blob]);
    const treeFile = path.join(h.home, 'duplicate-entries.tree');
    fs.writeFileSync(treeFile, Buffer.concat([entry, entry]));
    const tree = h.git(o, 'hash-object', '--literally', '-t', 'tree', '-w', treeFile);
    const bad = h.git(o, 'commit-tree', tree, '-p', 'refs/heads/main', '-m', 'malformed');
    h.git(o, 'update-ref', 'refs/heads/main', bad);
    const before = rev(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/main');
    const rec = plantGitRecorder(h.home);

    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: false, failure: 'fetch-rejected-objects', branch: 'main' });
    expect(rev(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/main')).toBe(before);
    const argv = fetchCalls(rec.calls()).map((c) => c.argv.join(' '));
    expect(argv).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(argv[0]).toContain('-c fetch.fsckObjects=true');
    expect(argv[0]).toContain('-c transfer.fsckObjects=true');

    // CONTROL: without the two fsck settings git takes the malformed object and moves the ref onto it.
    h.git(main, 'fetch', '-q', '--no-write-fetch-head', 'origin', '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main');
    expect(rev(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/main')).toBe(bad);
  });
});

describe('docs-fetch stamp and floor (row 43)', () => {
  it('ok writes okMs and okCommit; a later failure keeps them; files are 0600 and directories 0700', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    const next = advanceOrigin('demo');
    const t0 = Date.now();
    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: true, after: next, stamp: 'written' });
    const t1 = Date.now();
    const p = stampFile(main, 'main');
    const ok = readStampFile(p);
    expect(ok).toEqual({ v: 1, branch: 'main', attemptMs: ok.attemptMs, lastOutcome: 'ok', okMs: ok.attemptMs, okCommit: next });
    expect(ok.attemptMs).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(t0);
    expect(ok.attemptMs).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t1);
    expect(fs.statSync(p).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o600);
    for (const d of [path.dirname(p), path.dirname(path.dirname(p)), path.dirname(path.dirname(path.dirname(p)))]) {
      expect(fs.statSync(d).mode & 0o777, d).toBe(0o700);
    }
    expect(path.dirname(path.dirname(path.dirname(p)))).toBe(path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', 'docs'));

    ageStamp(p, 60_000);
    h.git(main, 'remote', 'set-url', 'origin', path.join(h.home, 'nowhere.git'));
    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: false, failure: 'fetch-transport' });
    const failed = readStampFile(p);
    expect(failed).toMatchObject({ v: 1, branch: 'main', lastOutcome: 'fetch-transport', okMs: ok.okMs, okCommit: next });
    expect(failed.attemptMs, 'the failed attempt is stamped as an attempt of its own').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(ok.attemptMs);
  });

  it('a second call within 10 s answers fetch-too-soon {retryAfterMs} with no fetch; the floor is per branch', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: true });
    const first = readStampFile(stampFile(main, 'main'));
    const rec = plantGitRecorder(h.home);
    const a = fetchDocs('demo');
    expect(a).toMatchObject({ v: 1, verb: 'docs-fetch', ok: false, failure: 'fetch-too-soon', branch: 'main' });
    expect(a['retryAfterMs'] as number).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(a['retryAfterMs'] as number).toBeLessThanOrEqual(10_000);
    expect(fetchCalls(rec.calls()), 'the floor answers before any network call').toEqual([]);
    expect(readStampFile(stampFile(main, 'main')), 'a refused call is not an attempt').toEqual(first);
    // Another branch of the same repository has a stamp, and so a floor, of its own.
    expect(fetchDocs('demo', 'nosuch')).toMatchObject({ ok: false, failure: 'remote-branch-absent' });
  });

  it('a stamp from the future (the clock stepped back) holds no floor, and is rewritten', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    const p = stampFile(main, 'main');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(p), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    const ahead = Date.now() + 3_600_000;
    fs.writeFileSync(p, JSON.stringify({ v: 1, branch: 'main', attemptMs: ahead, lastOutcome: 'ok', okMs: ahead,
      okCommit: rev(main, 'refs/remotes/origin/main') }));
    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: true, stamp: 'written' });
    expect(readStampFile(p).attemptMs).toBeLessThan(ahead);
  });

  it('a FIFO at the stamp path neither hangs the call nor is opened: it is replaced', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    const p = stampFile(main, 'main');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(p), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    execFileSync('mkfifo', [p]);
    // A unit, not the dispatcher: its spawn carries a timeout, so a regression is a red test rather than a hang.
    const a = unitJson<Answer>(h.home, fetchUnit('demo'), { timeoutMs: 30_000 });
    expect(a).toMatchObject({ ok: true, stamp: 'written' });
    expect(fs.lstatSync(p).isFile()).toBe(true);
    expect(readStampFile(p)).toMatchObject({ v: 1, branch: 'main', lastOutcome: 'ok' });
  });

  it('a symlink at the stamp path is replaced, never written through: its target is unchanged', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    const p = stampFile(main, 'main');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(p), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    const victim = path.join(h.home, 'victim');
    fs.writeFileSync(victim, 'victim\n');
    fs.symlinkSync(victim, p);
    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: true, stamp: 'written' });
    expect(fs.readFileSync(victim, 'utf8')).toBe('victim\n');
    expect(fs.lstatSync(p).isSymbolicLink()).toBe(false);
    expect(readStampFile(p)).toMatchObject({ lastOutcome: 'ok' });
  });

  it('a symlinked stamp directory refuses the write: stamp unwritten, and nothing lands where it points', () => {
    h.makeRepo('demo');
    const elsewhere = path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere');
    fs.mkdirSync(elsewhere);
    fs.symlinkSync(elsewhere, path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', 'docs'));
    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: true, moved: 'unchanged', stamp: 'unwritten' });
    expect(fs.readdirSync(elsewhere)).toEqual([]);
    expect(fs.lstatSync(path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', 'docs')).isSymbolicLink()).toBe(true);
  });

  it('$REG/docs is invisible to the registry globs and to _reg_purge', () => {
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    expect(fetchDocs('demo')).toMatchObject({ ok: true, stamp: 'written' });
    const p = stampFile(main, 'main');
    const globbed = h.sh('_reg_set demo-a uuid abc; _reg_set demo-a project demo; shopt -s nullglob; '
      + 'printf "%s\\n" "$REG"/*.uuid "$REG"/*.workspace "$REG"/*.project').split('\n').filter((l) => l !== '');
    expect(globbed).toEqual([path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', 'demo-a.uuid'), path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', 'demo-a.project')]);
    h.sh('_reg_purge demo-a');
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', 'demo-a.uuid')), 'the purge ran').toBe(false);
    expect(readStampFile(p)).toMatchObject({ v: 1, branch: 'main', lastOutcome: 'ok' });
  });
});

Replace with:

````python
# docs-fetch (spec 2026-10-01 section 2 (g) steps 1-9): ONE branch from origin
# into refs/remotes/origin/<b>, and nothing else. In order: discovery (a
# partial clone is refused there), the origin check, the branch, the floor
# (read from the stamp, before any network call), `before`, the fetch, the
# classifier, `after`, the stamp. There is NO ccd lock: git's own ref lock
# arbitrates two fetches of one ref (the loser answers ref-locked), and the
# server single-flights its own callers.
import errno
import json
import os
import re

# Step 6's line. docs_git(fetch=True) writes FETCH_PREFIX first (`git
# --no-pager -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false`), then these
# -c pairs, then `-C <M>`, then the subcommand, so the argv git receives is the
# spec's line byte for byte; ccd-docs-fetch.test.ts compares the recorded argv
# with that line. --no-optional-locks belongs to the READ runner and is not on
# it. The two fsck pairs make git REFUSE a malformed object rather than write
# it into a store live sessions share (R16 is the price: a remote holding such
# an object is refused on every fetch of that branch).
FETCH_ARGV_HEAD=('-c','gc.auto=0','-c','maintenance.auto=false','-c','fetch.writeCommitGraph=false','-c','submodule.recurse=false','-c','fetch.recurseSubmodules=false','-c','fetch.fsckObjects=true','-c','transfer.fsckObjects=true')
# --no-write-fetch-head leaves a worker's FETCH_HEAD alone; --no-tags and the
# one explicit refspec move exactly one ref; the leading `+` matches git's
# default refspec, so a force-pushed ws/* branch does not stay stale. The
# refspec itself is appended per call: +refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/origin/<b>.
# The branch reached the helper through the bare-ref grammar, which admits no
# `:`, `+`, `*`, `^` or `~`, so it cannot widen the refspec.
FETCH_SUBCOMMAND = ('fetch', '--quiet', '--no-tags', '--no-prune', '--no-recurse-submodules',
                    '--no-write-fetch-head', '--no-auto-gc', '--no-auto-maintenance',
                    '--no-show-forced-updates', '--end-of-options', 'origin')
FETCH_TRACKED_PREFIX = 'refs/remotes/origin/'

# Step 7's evidence: git's own English, which the fetch env pins with LC_ALL=C.
# Each one was measured on git 2.43.0; whether a translated locale changes them
# is UNMEASURED (R6), and a git that rewords one degrades that word toward
# fetch-transport or fetch-failed, never to another specific word.
FETCH_ABSENT_MARK = "couldn't find remote ref"
# git's fsck refusal is two facts at once: the pack step failed (index-pack, or
# unpack-objects) AND an fsck error is named, either index-pack's own "fsck
# error in packed object" or the reporter's `error: object <oid>: <msgId>: <text>`
# line. Measured: both fetch-pack's "invalid index-pack output" and a plain
# "index-pack failed" carry both.
FETCH_FSCK_PACK_RE = r'index-pack|unpack-objects'
FETCH_FSCK_ERROR_RE = r'fsck error in pack|^error: object [0-9a-f]{40}(?:[0-9a-f]{24})?: [A-Za-z]+: '
FETCH_AUTH_MARKS = ('Authentication failed', 'could not read Username', 'Permission denied (publickey)')
FETCH_LOCK_MARK = 'cannot lock ref'

# A failure's `detail` (the envelope's bound, section 2 (b)): redacted BEFORE it
# is cut, so a cut never slides a secret out from under a pattern's length floor.
FETCH_DETAIL_BYTES = 2048

# The stamp's own directories under $REG: docs, fetch and <repo key>. $REG is
# ccd's (`mkdir -p "$REG"` runs on every ccd start) and is opened as ccd opens
# it; each of these three is created at 0700 and opened with O_NOFOLLOW, so a
# symlink in any of them refuses the write rather than following it.
FETCH_STAMP_DIRS = 3
FETCH_STAMP_DIR_MODE = 0o700
FETCH_STAMP_FILE_MODE = 0o600


def classify_fetch(rc, stderr, timed_out):
    """Step 7's table, in its order: None for a fetch that exited 0, else the
    one word. Pure. rc is None only when nothing ran (a spent deadline, which
    arrives as timed_out); stderr is already decoded."""
    if timed_out:
        return 'fetch-timeout'
    if rc == 0:
        return None
    if rc == 128 and FETCH_ABSENT_MARK in stderr:
        return 'remote-branch-absent'
    if re.search(FETCH_FSCK_PACK_RE, stderr) and re.search(FETCH_FSCK_ERROR_RE, stderr, re.M):
        return 'fetch-rejected-objects'
    if any(m in stderr for m in FETCH_AUTH_MARKS):
        return 'fetch-auth-failed'
    if rc == 1 and FETCH_LOCK_MARK in stderr:
        return 'ref-locked'
    if rc == 128:
        return 'fetch-transport'
    return 'fetch-failed'


def lock_age_ms(repo, branch):
    """Fleet now minus the mtime of <common-dir>/refs/remotes/origin/<b>.lock,
    in ms and never negative, or None when that lock has already gone. Any
    other lstat failure is RAISED: "gone" and "could not look" are two answers
    with two remedies, and verb_fetch answers the second by leaving lockAgeMs
    out rather than folding it into null."""
    p = os.path.join(repo.common_dir, 'refs', 'remotes', 'origin', *branch.split('/')) + '.lock'
    try:
        st = SYS.lstat(p)
    except OSError as e:
        if e.errno in (errno.ENOENT, errno.ENOTDIR):
            return None
        raise
    return max(0, SYS.now_ms() - st.st_mtime_ns // 1000000)


def fetch_detail(err):
    """A fetch's stderr for `detail`: decoded, redacted, stripped, and only
    then cut to FETCH_DETAIL_BYTES on a code point boundary."""
    s = redact(err.decode('utf-8', 'replace')).strip()
    return s.encode('utf-8')[:FETCH_DETAIL_BYTES].decode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def tracked_oid(repo, ref, dl):
    """The object `ref` names, or None when it is absent: one for-each-ref,
    read by the EXACT refname (MM3), as steps 5 and 8 say. docs_git itself
    answers a spent bound (git-timeout) and an overflow."""
    r = docs_git(repo.path, ['for-each-ref', '--format=' + FER_FORMAT, '--end-of-options', ref],
                 call_s=CALL_S['ref'], dl=dl, ceiling=ceiling_of(repo.path))
    if r.rc != 0:
        raise fail('git-failed', step='for-each-ref', rc=r.rc, stderrHead=stderr_head(r.err))
    row = parse_for_each_ref(r.out).get(ref)
    return None if row is None else row[1]


def write_stamp(path, obj):
    """Write the stamp `obj` at `path` (stamp_path's shape: $REG/docs/fetch/
    <key>/<leaf>.json) and say whether it landed. Every missing one of the
    stamp's three directories is created at 0700, and each is opened with
    O_NOFOLLOW, so a symlinked one refuses the write. The bytes go to a fresh
    file in the same directory (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, a random name, mode 0600:
    mkstemp's contract, under the directory descriptor already opened) and
    are renamed over the leaf with os.replace, which replaces a FIFO or a
    symlink planted there and never opens it. Any failure removes the
    temporary file and answers False, which the verb reports as
    stamp:'unwritten'."""
    leaf = os.path.basename(path)
    names = []
    base = os.path.dirname(path)
    for _ in range(FETCH_STAMP_DIRS):
        names.insert(0, os.path.basename(base))
        base = os.path.dirname(base)
    fds = []
    tmp = None
    try:
        fds.append(os.open(base, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_CLOEXEC))
        for name in names:
            try:
                os.mkdir(name, FETCH_STAMP_DIR_MODE, dir_fd=fds[-1])
            except FileExistsError:
                pass
            fds.append(os.open(name, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC,
                               dir_fd=fds[-1]))
        data = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')
        tmp = '.%s.%s.tmp' % (leaf, os.urandom(8).hex())
        fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC,
                     FETCH_STAMP_FILE_MODE, dir_fd=fds[-1])
        try:
            os.fchmod(fd, FETCH_STAMP_FILE_MODE)
            while data:
                data = data[os.write(fd, data):]
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
        os.replace(tmp, leaf, src_dir_fd=fds[-1], dst_dir_fd=fds[-1])
        tmp = None
        return True
    except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError):
        if tmp is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp, dir_fd=fds[-1])
            except OSError:
                pass
        return False
    finally:
        for fd in fds:
            os.close(fd)


def verb_fetch(ctx, a, fetch_s=CALL_S['fetch'], total_s=HELPER_DEADLINE_S['docs-fetch']):
    """DocsFetchOk's body {branch, trackedRef, defaultVia?, before, after,
    moved, stamp}, or a failure word. fetch_s and total_s are the fetch's own
    bound and the helper deadline: VERBS calls this with both defaults, and a
    unit lowers one by passing it (no env knob, no argv flag)."""
    dl = Deadline(total_s)
    repo = discover(ctx, a.project, dl)
    if origin_url(repo, dl) is None:
        raise fail('remote-absent')
    branch, via = a.branch, None
    if branch is None:
        picked = default_branch_name(repo, dl)
        if picked is None:
            raise fail('no-default-branch')
        branch, via = picked
    tracked = FETCH_TRACKED_PREFIX + branch
    path = stamp_path(ctx.reg, repo.key, branch)
    prior = read_stamp(path)
    if prior is not None and prior['branch'] != branch:
        prior = None
    if prior is not None:
        # The floor reads attemptMs, which every attempt writes. A stamp from
        # the future (the fleet clock stepped back) holds no floor: this
        # attempt rewrites it, where honouring it would refuse every fetch of
        # this branch for as long as the step.
        age = SYS.now_ms() - prior['attemptMs']
        if 0 <= age < DOCS_FETCH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS:
            raise fail('fetch-too-soon', branch=branch, retryAfterMs=DOCS_FETCH_MIN_INTERVAL_MS - age)
    before = tracked_oid(repo, tracked, dl)
    attempt_ms = SYS.now_ms()
    args = list(FETCH_ARGV_HEAD) + list(FETCH_SUBCOMMAND) + ['+refs/heads/%s:%s' % (branch, tracked)]
    r = docs_git(repo.path, args, call_s=fetch_s, dl=dl, ceiling=ceiling_of(repo.path),
                 fetch=True, soft=True)
    word = classify_fetch(r.rc, r.err.decode('utf-8', 'replace'), r.timed_out)
    if word is None:
        after = tracked_oid(repo, tracked, dl)
        if after is None:
            raise fail('git-failed', step='for-each-ref',
                       detail=tracked + ' is absent after a fetch that exited 0')
        written = write_stamp(path, {'v': 1, 'branch': branch, 'attemptMs': attempt_ms,
                                     'lastOutcome': 'ok', 'okMs': attempt_ms, 'okCommit': after})
        body = {'branch': branch, 'trackedRef': tracked}
        if via is not None:
            body['defaultVia'] = via
        body['before'] = before
        body['after'] = after
        body['moved'] = 'created' if before is None else ('unchanged' if before == after else 'updated')
        body['stamp'] = 'written' if written else 'unwritten'
        return body
    # A failed attempt is still an attempt: it is stamped, carrying the last
    # success over, and the failure body itself has no `stamp` field.
    write_stamp(path, {'v': 1, 'branch': branch, 'attemptMs': attempt_ms, 'lastOutcome': word,
                       'okMs': None if prior is None else prior.get('okMs'),
                       'okCommit': None if prior is None else prior.get('okCommit')})
    fields = {'branch': branch}
    text = fetch_detail(r.err)
    if text:
        fields['detail'] = text
    if word == 'ref-locked':
        try:
            fields['lockAgeMs'] = lock_age_ms(repo, branch)
        except OSError:
            pass
    elif word in ('fetch-transport', 'fetch-failed'):
        fields['stderrHead'] = stderr_head(r.err)
        if word == 'fetch-failed':
            fields['rc'] = r.rc
    raise fail(word, **fields)
````

The replacement ends at `raise fail(word, **fields)`. T6's blank line and `# ===== docs: entry =====` follow it unchanged, and `VERBS` still binds `'docs-fetch'` to `verb_fetch` by name.

- [ ] **Step 3: The mutation table.** Mutations never run in the worktree. `mutate.py` builds `<SCRATCH>/w1-mut`, a `git archive` copy of HEAD whose `server/node_modules` is a symlink to the worktree's (measured while planning: vitest runs from such a copy). It refuses to start until every test file the rows name is green unmutated in that copy, so a test that needed something the copy lacks (the repository's own `.git`, say) shows up there, never as a red row. Then it applies one row at a time, restamps a mutated `ccd/ccd` (so no stamp check can stand in for a guard pin), and refuses a mutated helper that no longer parses at `feature_version=(3, 8)` or no longer imports (UNPARSEABLE, never red). It runs the row's test files with `--bail=1` and restores the file byte for byte, from the row's own backup, checked against the manifest's sha256. A run killed mid-row leaves `w1-mut.pending.json`; the next invocation restores from it, and stops that row's vitest group, before anything else. The runner's mechanics were exercised while planning, on rows over `shared/api.ts`: red, green, skipped, unparseable, SIGTERM and SIGKILL mid-row, and the final byte check.

Write the runner to `<SCRATCH>/mutate.py`:

````python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mutation runner for the native Docs reader, wave 1 (the plan's Task 19). Scratch only: never committed.

Run from the WORKTREE root. It reads HEAD with git, and it never writes inside the worktree:

  python3 mutate.py ROWS MUT setup             build MUT, a `git archive` copy of HEAD, and its manifest
  python3 mutate.py ROWS MUT baseline          every test file the rows name, unmutated, one at a time: all green
  python3 mutate.py ROWS MUT run [ID ...]      measure the rows not measured yet (all of them, or the IDs given)
  python3 mutate.py ROWS MUT final             MUT is byte-equal to HEAD again, and every test file is green again
  python3 mutate.py ROWS MUT report            the measured table, as markdown, for the PR body

ROWS is a JSON list of rows: {id, row, task, guard, pkg, file, old, new, tests, more?, expect?, timeoutIsRed?,
timeoutS?}. A row replaces exactly one occurrence of `old` with `new` in MUT/<file>, then each [old, new] pair in
`more`, in order; a pair whose `old` is absent or not unique SKIPS the row and touches nothing. `expect` is 'red'
(the default) or 'green' (an equivalent mutation, kept to show the spec's named mutation cannot bite here).

Each row backs its file up under a sentinel of its own (MUT.bak/<id>.orig plus the sha256 the manifest recorded),
writes MUT.pending.json BEFORE it mutates, and restores the file byte for byte afterwards, asserting the sha256.
A run killed mid-row leaves MUT.pending.json behind, and the next invocation restores from it before anything
else. A mutated ccd/ccd is re-stamped (so no stamp check can pass for a guard pin) and must pass `bash -n`; its
helper must parse at feature_version (3, 8) and import, or the row is UNPARSEABLE, never red.

One invocation starts a row or a file only while it has run less than BUDGET_S seconds AND that piece's own
vitest bound still ends before CEILING_S, so every invocation ends inside a 600 s tool call; a piece that does not
fit waits for the next invocation, where it starts first. Run it again until it prints ALL ROWS MEASURED (or ALL
FILES GREEN).
"""
import hashlib, json, os, re, shutil, signal, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time

BUDGET_S = 240
CEILING_S = 570
ROW_TIMEOUT_S = 330
FILE_TIMEOUT_S = 540
OPENER = "  python3 /dev/fd/3 \"$@\" 3<<'DOCS_PY'\n"
CLOSER = '\nDOCS_PY\n'
RESTAMP = ("import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'; const { markGenerated } = await import("
           "'./shared/mark.mjs'); writeFileSync('ccd/ccd', markGenerated(readFileSync('ccd/ccd', 'utf8')))")
IMPORT_CHECK = ("import importlib.util, sys\n"
                "s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('docs_helper', sys.argv[1])\n"
                "m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s)\n"
                "s.loader.exec_module(m)\n")
ANSI = re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]')


def die(msg):
    print('mutate.py: ' + msg, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def sha(b):
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


def on_signal(signum, _frame):
    raise SystemExit(128 + signum)


for _s in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGHUP):
    signal.signal(_s, on_signal)

if len(sys.argv) < 4:
    die(__doc__)
ROWS_PATH, MUT, CMD = sys.argv[1], os.path.abspath(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
ROOT = os.getcwd()
top = subprocess.run(['git', 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel'], capture_output=True, text=True)
if top.returncode != 0 or os.path.realpath(top.stdout.strip()) != os.path.realpath(ROOT):
    die('run me from the worktree root')
real_mut, real_root = os.path.realpath(MUT), os.path.realpath(ROOT)
if real_mut == real_root or real_mut.startswith(real_root + os.sep):
    die('MUT must lie OUTSIDE the worktree: mutations never run in it')
ROWS = json.load(open(ROWS_PATH, encoding='utf-8'))
BY_ID = dict((r['id'], r) for r in ROWS)
if len(BY_ID) != len(ROWS):
    die('duplicate row ids')
MANIFEST, RESULTS, PENDING, BAK = MUT + '.manifest.json', MUT + '.results.jsonl', MUT + '.pending.json', MUT + '.bak'
BASE_DONE, FINAL_DONE = MUT + '.baseline.json', MUT + '.final.json'
T0 = time.monotonic()


def head_sha():
    return subprocess.run(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()


def head_bytes(f):
    return subprocess.run(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + f], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout


def load_manifest():
    if not os.path.exists(MANIFEST):
        die('no manifest: run setup first')
    m = json.load(open(MANIFEST))
    if m['head'] != head_sha():
        die('HEAD moved since setup: run setup, then baseline, again')
    return m


def restore_pending(m):
    if not os.path.exists(PENDING):
        return
    p = json.load(open(PENDING))
    if p.get('pgid') and ours(p['pgid']):
        kill_group(p['pgid'])
    shutil.copyfile(p['bak'], os.path.join(MUT, p['file']))
    got = sha(open(os.path.join(MUT, p['file']), 'rb').read())
    if got != m['files'][p['file']]:
        die('restore of %s from %s did not give the manifest bytes' % (p['file'], p['bak']))
    os.remove(p['bak'])
    os.remove(PENDING)
    print('restored %s, left mutated by an interrupted row %s' % (p['file'], p['id']))


def assert_pristine(m):
    for f, want in sorted(m['files'].items()):
        if sha(open(os.path.join(MUT, f), 'rb').read()) != want:
            die('%s in MUT is not the HEAD bytes: run setup again' % f)


def kill_group(pgid):
    """SIGTERM to vitest's whole process group (its workers, the ccd and python they spawned), then SIGKILL."""
    for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGKILL):
        try:
            os.killpg(pgid, sig)
        except OSError:
            return
        if sig == signal.SIGTERM:
            time.sleep(5)


def ours(pid):
    """True only while pid is still a vitest leader running in MUT: a recorded pid can be reused once its process
    has gone, and this runner never signals a group it cannot prove is its own."""
    try:
        cwd = os.path.realpath('/proc/%d/cwd' % pid)
    except OSError:
        return False
    return cwd == real_mut or cwd.startswith(real_mut + os.sep)


def vitest(pkg, files, timeout_s, bail, on_start=None):
    argv = ['./node_modules/.bin/vitest', 'run'] + (['--bail=1'] if bail else []) + list(files)
    p = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=os.path.join(MUT, pkg), stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                         start_new_session=True)
    if on_start is not None:
        on_start(p.pid)
    try:
        out, _ = p.communicate(timeout=timeout_s)
        return p.returncode, ANSI.sub('', out.decode('utf-8', 'replace')), False
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        kill_group(p.pid)
        out, _ = p.communicate()
        return None, ANSI.sub('', out.decode('utf-8', 'replace')), True
    except BaseException:
        kill_group(p.pid)
        raise


def classify(rc, out, timed_out):
    """green | red | timeout | error. Red needs a FAILED TEST: a file that fails to load (a mutation that broke
    the module rather than a guard), a config error or 'no test files' is error, never red."""
    if timed_out:
        return 'timeout', out.strip()[-600:]
    if rc == 0:
        return 'green', ''
    lines = out.splitlines()
    named = [l.strip() for l in lines if re.match(r'^\s*(FAIL|\u00d7|\u2717)\s', l) and ' > ' in l]
    counted = re.findall(r'^\s*Tests\s+(\d+) failed', out, re.M)
    if named or (counted and int(counted[-1]) > 0):
        return 'red', (named[0] if named else 'Tests %s failed' % counted[-1])[:240]
    return 'error', out.strip()[-1200:]


def check_ccd(path):
    """None when the mutated ccd/ccd still parses as bash and its helper parses at 3.8 and imports; else why."""
    r = subprocess.run(['bash', '-n', path], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return 'bash -n: ' + r.stderr.strip()[:300]
    text = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    if text.count(OPENER) != 1:
        return 'the helper opener is not unique'
    a = text.index(OPENER) + len(OPENER)
    b = text.find(CLOSER, a)
    if b < 0:
        return 'the helper terminator is missing'
    src = text[a:b + 1]
    import ast
    try:
        ast.parse(src, feature_version=(3, 8))
    except SyntaxError as e:
        return 'helper SyntaxError: %s' % e
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', suffix='.py', delete=False, encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        fh.write(src)
        tmp = fh.name
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(['python3', '-c', IMPORT_CHECK, tmp], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    finally:
        os.remove(tmp)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return 'helper import: ' + r.stderr.strip()[-300:]
    return None


def results():
    got = {}
    if os.path.exists(RESULTS):
        for line in open(RESULTS, encoding='utf-8'):
            if line.strip():
                o = json.loads(line)
                got[o['id']] = o
    return got


def all_files():
    seen = []
    for r in ROWS:
        for t in r['tests']:
            key = (r.get('pkg', 'server'), t)
            if key not in seen:
                seen.append(key)
    return seen


def cmd_setup():
    for p in (MUT, BAK):
        if os.path.exists(p):
            shutil.rmtree(p)
    for p in (MANIFEST, RESULTS, PENDING, BASE_DONE, FINAL_DONE):
        if os.path.exists(p):
            os.remove(p)
    os.makedirs(MUT)
    os.makedirs(BAK)
    tar = subprocess.run(['git', 'archive', '--format=tar', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    subprocess.run(['tar', '-x', '-C', MUT], input=tar, check=True)
    for pkg in sorted(set(r.get('pkg', 'server') for r in ROWS)):
        src = os.path.join(ROOT, pkg, 'node_modules')
        if not os.path.isdir(src):
            die('%s has no node_modules: run npm ci there first' % pkg)
        os.symlink(src, os.path.join(MUT, pkg, 'node_modules'))
    files = {}
    for f in sorted(set(r['file'] for r in ROWS)):
        data = open(os.path.join(MUT, f), 'rb').read()
        if data != head_bytes(f):
            die('%s in the archive differs from HEAD' % f)
        files[f] = sha(data)
    json.dump({'head': head_sha(), 'files': files}, open(MANIFEST, 'w'), indent=1)
    print('MUT ready at HEAD %s: %d files under mutation, %d rows, %d test files'
          % (head_sha()[:12], len(files), len(ROWS), len(all_files())))


def fits(tmo):
    """May a piece bounded by tmo seconds start now?"""
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - T0
    return elapsed <= BUDGET_S and elapsed + tmo <= CEILING_S


def run_files(done_path, label):
    m = load_manifest()
    restore_pending(m)
    assert_pristine(m)
    done = json.load(open(done_path)) if os.path.exists(done_path) else {}
    for pkg, f in all_files():
        key = pkg + ':' + f
        if done.get(key) == 'green':
            continue
        if not fits(FILE_TIMEOUT_S):
            print('%d of %d files green; run `%s` again' % (len(done), len(all_files()), label))
            return 3
        rc, out, timed_out = vitest(pkg, [f], FILE_TIMEOUT_S, False)
        verdict, detail = classify(rc, out, timed_out)
        print('%-8s %s %s' % (verdict.upper(), key, detail[:300]))
        if verdict != 'green':
            print(out.strip()[-2000:])
            die('%s is not green unmutated: every red row would be meaningless; stop and report' % key)
        done[key] = 'green'
        json.dump(done, open(done_path, 'w'), indent=1)
    print('ALL FILES GREEN (%s)' % label)
    return 0


def mutate_one(m, r):
    f = r['file']
    path = os.path.join(MUT, f)
    orig = open(path, 'rb').read()
    text = orig.decode('utf-8')
    for old, new in [(r['old'], r['new'])] + [tuple(x) for x in r.get('more', [])]:
        n = text.count(old)
        if n != 1:
            return 'skipped', '`old` occurs %d times in %s: %r' % (n, f, old[:80])
        text = text.replace(old, new, 1)
    bak = os.path.join(BAK, r['id'] + '.orig')
    shutil.copyfile(path, bak)
    pending = {'id': r['id'], 'file': f, 'bak': bak}
    json.dump(pending, open(PENDING, 'w'))

    def started(pid):
        pending['pgid'] = pid
        json.dump(pending, open(PENDING, 'w'))

    try:
        open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(text)
        if f == 'ccd/ccd':
            subprocess.run(['node', '--input-type=module', '-e', RESTAMP], cwd=MUT, check=True)
            why = check_ccd(path)
            if why is not None:
                return 'unparseable', why
        elif f.startswith('ccd/'):
            p = subprocess.run(['bash', '-n', path], capture_output=True, text=True)
            if p.returncode != 0:
                return 'unparseable', 'bash -n: ' + p.stderr.strip()[:300]
        rc, out, timed_out = vitest(r.get('pkg', 'server'), r['tests'], r.get('timeoutS', ROW_TIMEOUT_S), True,
                                    started)
        return classify(rc, out, timed_out)
    finally:
        shutil.copyfile(bak, path)
        if sha(open(path, 'rb').read()) != m['files'][f]:
            die('%s was not restored byte for byte after row %s (backup kept at %s)' % (f, r['id'], bak))
        os.remove(bak)
        os.remove(PENDING)


def ok_of(r, verdict):
    if r.get('expect', 'red') == 'green':
        return verdict == 'green'
    return verdict == 'red' or (verdict == 'timeout' and bool(r.get('timeoutIsRed')))


def cmd_run(ids):
    m = load_manifest()
    restore_pending(m)
    assert_pristine(m)
    for i in ids:
        if i not in BY_ID:
            die('no row %s' % i)
    got = results()
    queue = [r for r in ROWS if r['id'] in ids] if ids else [r for r in ROWS if r['id'] not in got]
    bad = 0
    for r in queue:
        if not fits(r.get('timeoutS', ROW_TIMEOUT_S)):
            continue
        t = time.monotonic()
        verdict, detail = mutate_one(m, r)
        ok = ok_of(r, verdict)
        rec = {'id': r['id'], 'verdict': verdict, 'ok': ok, 'detail': detail, 'seconds': int(time.monotonic() - t)}
        with open(RESULTS, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(rec) + '\n')
        bad += 0 if ok else 1
        print('== %-12s [row %s, %s] %-11s %s  %ss  %s' % (r['id'], r['row'], r['task'], verdict.upper(),
              'ok' if ok else 'NOT OK', rec['seconds'], detail[:200]))
    assert_pristine(m)
    left = [x['id'] for x in ROWS if x['id'] not in results()]
    if left:
        print('%d rows left (%s...): run `run` again' % (len(left), ', '.join(left[:6])))
        return 3
    nok = [x for x in results().values() if not x['ok']]
    print('ALL ROWS MEASURED: %d ok, %d not ok%s' % (len(ROWS) - len(nok), len(nok),
          (' -> ' + ', '.join(x['id'] for x in nok)) if nok else ''))
    return 1 if (nok or bad) else 0


def cmd_final():
    m = load_manifest()
    restore_pending(m)
    for f, want in sorted(m['files'].items()):
        got = open(os.path.join(MUT, f), 'rb').read()
        if sha(got) != want or got != head_bytes(f):
            die('%s in MUT is not byte-equal to HEAD' % f)
    print('MUT byte-equal to HEAD for all %d mutated files' % len(m['files']))
    return run_files(FINAL_DONE, 'final')


def cmd_report():
    got = results()
    out = ['| Row | Spec row | Task | Mutation | Result | First red case |', '|---|---|---|---|---|---|']
    for r in ROWS:
        g = got.get(r['id'])
        if g is None:
            res, case = 'NOT MEASURED', ''
        else:
            res = g['verdict'] + ('' if g['ok'] else ' (NOT OK)')
            case = g['detail'] if g['verdict'] == 'red' else ''
        cell = lambda s: s.replace('|', '\\|').replace('\n', ' ')
        out.append('| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |' % (r['id'], r['row'], r['task'], cell(r['guard']), res,
                                                      cell(case[:160])))
    nok = [r['id'] for r in ROWS if r['id'] not in got or not got[r['id']]['ok']]
    out.append('')
    out.append('%d rows; %d measured as expected%s.' % (len(ROWS), len(ROWS) - len(nok),
               ('; not as expected or not measured: ' + ', '.join(nok)) if nok else ''))
    print('\n'.join(out))
    return 0


if CMD == 'setup':
    cmd_setup()
    sys.exit(0)
if CMD == 'baseline':
    sys.exit(run_files(BASE_DONE, 'baseline'))
if CMD == 'run':
    if not os.path.exists(BASE_DONE) or len(json.load(open(BASE_DONE))) != len(all_files()):
        die('run `baseline` to ALL FILES GREEN first')
    sys.exit(cmd_run(sys.argv[4:]))
if CMD == 'final':
    sys.exit(cmd_final())
if CMD == 'report':
    sys.exit(cmd_report())
die('unknown command %r' % CMD)
````

Write the rows to `<SCRATCH>/w1-rows.json`. One row per guard of spec 2026-10-01 rows 1-43, 45 (ccd half), 48, 53 (L0), 55-59, 61 and 62 (ccd half), 63-65, M3.1-M3.3, M3.11, M3.12, M5.3, M5.7, M6.6-M6.8, M7.3 (TS half), M7.4, M7.6 and M7.8 (row 6). Where the spec names more than one mutation ("each mutated alone", "drop either"), each is its own row. Each mutation is the spec's "mutation that goes red", written against the text its task ships. Four rows need a word:
- **R4b** is the spec's row-4 mutation itself, "drop `--full-tree`". Every git call this helper makes runs with `-C <the project's toplevel>`, so the flag alone changes no listing; the row is red because Task 10's `makes ONE git call, the fixed ls-tree over the four section paths` case pins the literal `ls-tree` argv (Task 10's own table measured this mutation red as `t10-fulltree`). Row 4's grammar half is pinned by R4a. The spec's other row-4 mutation, `<commit>:<path>`, cannot be written at all: `git_argv` refuses any `:` operand to `cat-file`, `ls-tree`, `rev-parse`, `merge-base` and `rev-list` (Task 8).
- **R16** adds a forbidden subcommand, `git remote`, to discovery, which every read verb runs. It goes through `SYS.spawn` because `docs_git`'s allowlist would refuse it first. The PATH recorder sees it, and the row-16 cases red in all three read-verb files.
- **R28** drops `O_NONBLOCK` from the leaf open. A FIFO then blocks the helper, so "red" is the row's vitest TIMING OUT (`timeoutIsRed`), exactly as spec row 28 says.
- **R37** turns the fingerprint into stat data in both places at once, the tree's `draft_facts` and show's pin check (`more`), so the two-edits-in-one-mtime-tick case is the one that reds.

Build the copy and prove it green, one Bash call per invocation, repeating `baseline` until it prints `ALL FILES GREEN (baseline)` (an invocation starts a file only while the file's 540 s bound still ends inside the tool call, so a large file waits for the next invocation, where it starts first):

```bash
SCRATCH=<abs path>; python3 "$SCRATCH/mutate.py" "$SCRATCH/w1-rows.json" "$SCRATCH/w1-mut" setup
SCRATCH=<abs path>; python3 "$SCRATCH/mutate.py" "$SCRATCH/w1-rows.json" "$SCRATCH/w1-mut" baseline
```

Expected: `MUT ready at HEAD <12 hex>: 4 files under mutation, 244 rows, 11 test files`, then one `GREEN    server:test/<file>` line per file across the invocations, ending `ALL FILES GREEN (baseline)`. A file that is not green unmutated stops the runner: run that same file in the worktree. If it is green there, the copy differs from the tree; stop and report. If it is red there too, it is a load flake or a real break: re-run it alone once, and stop and report if it stays red. Never run a row against a red baseline.

Then measure, one Bash call per invocation, repeating `run` (exit 3 means rows are left) until it prints `ALL ROWS MEASURED`:

```bash
SCRATCH=<abs path>; python3 "$SCRATCH/mutate.py" "$SCRATCH/w1-rows.json" "$SCRATCH/w1-mut" run
```

Each measured row prints `== <id> [row <spec row>, <task>] <VERDICT> ok|NOT OK <seconds>s <first red case>`, and the result is appended to `w1-mut.results.jsonl`, so an interrupted invocation loses at most the row in flight. Expected: every row `ok`. That is RED for all 244 rows (R28's red may come back as `TIMEOUT`, which its `timeoutIsRed` accepts). The owning tasks measured most of these mutations red in their own labs while planning: Tasks 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 13, 14 and 16 list theirs. A row that is `NOT OK`:
- **SKIPPED:** its `old` is not in the shipped file exactly once. Find the guard the row's `guard` names in the shipped file. If it is there with another spelling (a review round changed the task's text after this plan was written), rewrite that row's `old`/`new` in `w1-rows.json` as the SAME mutation of the shipped text, re-measure it alone (`python3 "$SCRATCH/mutate.py" "$SCRATCH/w1-rows.json" "$SCRATCH/w1-mut" run <ID>`), and add one line to `<SCRATCH>/w1-table-notes.md`: `- <ID>: re-anchored to the shipped text; same mutation.`. If the guard is gone, stop and report.
- **GREEN where red was expected:** a guard nothing pins. Re-measure it alone once. If it stays green, stop and report it with the row id: closing it is a test change in the owning task's file, and the coordinator orders that round.
- **TIMEOUT** without `timeoutIsRed`, or **ERROR:** re-measure it alone once. If it repeats, report it with the detail it printed; it is unmeasured, never red. An ERROR detail means the mutation broke the module rather than a guard (a test file that failed to load, or a config error).
- **UNPARSEABLE:** the row's text no longer leaves the helper or a bash file parseable. Report it; never count it.

Then prove the copy restored and green again, repeating `final` until it prints `ALL FILES GREEN (final)`, and prove the worktree untouched:

```bash
SCRATCH=<abs path>; python3 "$SCRATCH/mutate.py" "$SCRATCH/w1-rows.json" "$SCRATCH/w1-mut" final
git status --short
```

Expected: `MUT byte-equal to HEAD for all 4 mutated files`, the `GREEN` lines, `ALL FILES GREEN (final)`, and no status line.

- [ ] **Step 6: R3, the lab measurement (spec section 7.8).** Never against a live repository or the live HOME: the live checkout is only READ, by one `git worktree list` per project and one `git clone --shared` (which borrows the object store through `objects/info/alternates` and writes nothing to it). Everything else happens in a fixture HOME that the same harness every ccd test uses builds and removes.

Pick the fleet project with the most worktree records, and prove the temp root can hold two full checkouts of it, the clone's own and the holder's (the other records are added without a checkout, Step 6b). The project's NAME is never printed and never goes in the PR; `r3.env` lives in the scratchpad only:

```bash
SCRATCH=<abs path>
( set -eu
  best=""; bestn=0
  for g in "$HOME"/projects/*/.git; do
    [ -d "$g" ] || continue
    p="${g%/.git}"
    n="$(git --no-optional-locks -C "$p" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^worktree ' || true)"
    if [ "${n:-0}" -gt "$bestn" ]; then best="$p"; bestn="$n"; fi
  done
  [ -n "$best" ] || { echo 'no project with a .git directory under $HOME/projects: stop and report' >&2; exit 1; }
  tracked="$(git --no-optional-locks -C "$best" ls-tree -r -l HEAD | awk '$4 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $4 } END { print s + 0 }')"
  free="$(df -Pk "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" | awk 'NR == 2 { print $4 * 1024 }')"
  echo "worktree records: $bestn; tracked bytes per checkout: $tracked; free bytes in the temp root: $free"
  [ "$free" -gt $(( tracked * 3 + 1073741824 )) ] || { echo 'not enough room for two checkouts: stop and report R3 as not run' >&2; exit 1; }
  printf 'R3_SOURCE=%q\nR3_WORKTREES=%s\n' "$best" "$bestn" > "$SCRATCH/r3.env"
  echo 'r3.env written' )
```

Expected: the three counts, then `r3.env written`.

Step 6b. Write the lab to `<SCRATCH>/r3-lab.test.ts`. It runs only from the scratch copy, which Step 3 left byte-equal to HEAD, so the `ccd/ccd` it times is this branch's own:

````ts
// R3 (spec 2026-10-01 section 7.8), the plan's Task 19 lab. SCRATCH ONLY: this file lives in the mutation copy,
// never in the worktree, and is never committed. The live checkout named by R3_SOURCE is read once, by
// `git clone --shared`, which borrows its object store through objects/info/alternates and writes nothing to it.
// Everything else happens in a fixture HOME built by the harness every ccd test uses.
import { it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks';
import { makeCcdHarness } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { runCcdDocs, parseOneLine, plantGitRecorder } from './ccdDocsHelpers.js';
import { unitJson } from './docsHelperPy.js';

const SRC = process.env['R3_SOURCE'] ?? '';
const RECORDS = Number(process.env['R3_WORKTREES'] ?? '0');
const OUT = process.env['R3_OUT'] ?? '';
const SECTIONS = ['docs/superpowers/specs', 'docs/superpowers/plans', 'docs/product-design', 'docs/conventions'];
const HELD = 'ws/r3-held';
const DIRTY = 36;
const SAFE_PATH = /^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$/;

it('R3: docs-tree on a shared clone of the fleet project with the most worktrees', () => {
  expect(SRC, 'R3_SOURCE names the live checkout').not.toBe('');
  expect(fs.statSync(path.join(SRC, '.git')).isDirectory()).toBe(true);
  expect(Number.isInteger(RECORDS) && RECORDS >= 1).toBe(true);
  const h = makeCcdHarness('ccd-docs-');
  try {
    const projects = path.join(h.home, 'projects');
    const worktrees = path.join(h.home, 'worktrees');
    fs.mkdirSync(projects, { recursive: true });
    fs.mkdirSync(worktrees, { recursive: true });
    const m = path.join(projects, 'r3');
    h.git(projects, 'clone', '--quiet', '--shared', SRC, 'r3');

    // The holder, checked out in full, where a ws-add workspace would sit; then the other records, so that
    // `worktree list` in the clone counts what it counts on the live checkout. The others are not checked out:
    // nothing on docs-tree's path reads a non-holder's files (the list reads its record; only Bd's holder is
    // opened), and two full checkouts are all the temp root has to hold.
    const holder = path.join(worktrees, 'r3-held');
    h.git(m, 'worktree', 'add', '--quiet', '-b', HELD, holder, 'HEAD');
    const want = Math.max(RECORDS, 2);
    for (let i = 0; i < want - 2; i++) {
      h.git(m, 'worktree', 'add', '--quiet', '--no-checkout', '-b', `ws/r3-${i}`, path.join(worktrees, `r3-${i}`), 'HEAD');
    }
    const records = h.git(m, 'worktree', 'list', '--porcelain').split('\n').filter((l) => l.startsWith('worktree ')).length;
    expect(records).toBe(want);

    // 36 dirty docs in the holder: tracked regular files under the four sections first, then new files in specs.
    const listed = execFileSync('git', ['-C', holder, 'ls-files', '-s', '-z', '--', ...SECTIONS],
      { encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, HOME: h.home }, maxBuffer: 1 << 26 })
      .split('\0').filter(Boolean)
      .map((rec) => ({ mode: rec.slice(0, 6), p: rec.slice(rec.indexOf('\t') + 1) }))
      .filter((x) => (x.mode === '100644' || x.mode === '100755') && SAFE_PATH.test(x.p))
      .map((x) => x.p)
      .sort();
    const modified = listed.slice(0, DIRTY);
    for (const p of modified) fs.appendFileSync(path.join(holder, p), '\nr3 lab draft line\n');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(holder, SECTIONS[0]!), { recursive: true });
    for (let k = modified.length; k < DIRTY; k++) {
      fs.writeFileSync(path.join(holder, SECTIONS[0]!, `r3-lab-draft-${k}.md`), 'r3 lab draft\n');
    }

    // Once cold, then ten times warm, through the real dispatcher.
    const args = ['docs-tree', '--project', 'r3', '--ref', HELD];
    const timed = (): { ms: number; o: Record<string, unknown> } => {
      const t0 = performance.now();
      const r = runCcdDocs(h, args);
      const ms = Math.round(performance.now() - t0);
      return { ms, o: parseOneLine(r) };
    };
    const cold = timed();
    expect(cold.o['ok'], JSON.stringify(cold.o).slice(0, 2000)).toBe(true);
    expect((cold.o['drafts'] as Record<string, unknown>)['state']).toBe('holder');
    const entries = cold.o['entries'] as { committed: unknown; draft: unknown }[];
    expect(entries.filter((e) => e.draft !== null)).toHaveLength(DIRTY);
    const warm: number[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
      const w = timed();
      expect(w.o['ok']).toBe(true);
      warm.push(w.ms);
    }
    const sorted = [...warm].sort((a, b) => a - b);
    const p95 = sorted[Math.ceil(0.95 * sorted.length) - 1]!;

    // The draft phase degrades and the listing survives: status sleeps past a lowered per-call bound (call_s, a
    // function parameter with a production default; no env knob or argv flag exists for it).
    plantGitRecorder(h.home, { sleepWhen: ['status --porcelain=v2'], sleepS: 5 });
    const py = (s: string): string => JSON.stringify(s);
    const deg = unitJson<{ entries: number; drafts: Record<string, unknown> }>(h.home, [
      `ctx = H.Ctx('docs-tree', ${py(projects)}, ${py(worktrees)}, ${py(path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions'))}, H.SYS.monotonic())`,
      'dl = H.Deadline(60)',
      "repo = H.discover(ctx, 'r3', dl)",
      `ref = H.resolve(repo, ${py(HELD)}, dl)`,
      "sections, listing, unlisted, blobs = H.list_committed(repo, ref['commit'], dl)",
      "ph = H.draft_phase(ctx, repo, ref['name'], ref, blobs, dl, call_s=1)",
      "out({'entries': len(listing), 'drafts': ph.facts})",
    ].join('\n'), { timeoutMs: 120_000 });
    expect(deg.drafts).toMatchObject({ state: 'unreadable', step: 'status', detail: 'timeout' });
    expect(deg.entries).toBe(entries.filter((e) => e.committed !== null).length);

    const result = {
      records, dirty: DIRTY, modifiedTracked: modified.length, entries: entries.length,
      coldMs: cold.ms, warmMs: warm, warmP95Ms: p95, pass: cold.ms <= 8000 && p95 <= 2000,
      degraded: deg.drafts, listingSurvived: deg.entries,
    };
    if (OUT !== '') fs.writeFileSync(OUT, JSON.stringify(result, null, 1) + '\n');
    console.log('R3 ' + JSON.stringify(result));
  } finally {
    h.cleanup();
  }
}, 540_000);
````

The assertions are about correctness only: an `ok` answer, a `holder` drafts state with exactly 36 draft rows, and the degradation. The timing is recorded, never asserted. Over either bound is not a W1 failure: the PR body records the numbers, and the read-lane wait is re-derived from them before W3 merges. - [ ] **Step 7: Open the PR.** Write the body assembler to `<SCRATCH>/pr-body.py`:

````python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assemble the docs W1 pull request body from what Task 19 measured. Scratch only: never committed.

usage, from the worktree root: python3 pr-body.py <SCRATCH> <plan path> > <SCRATCH>/w1-pr-body.md
Reads <SCRATCH>/w1-suite-*.log, w1-cite.txt, w1-rows.json + the mutation results, r3-result.json, and the
optional w1-table-notes.md, w1-review-notes.md and w1-deviations.md. Every link is a GitHub blob URL: this body is read by people
who are not on any private network.
"""
import glob, json, os, re, subprocess, sys

S, PLAN = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
BLOB = 'https://github.com/Synapsium-Labs/ccrc-pwa/blob/main/'
SPEC = 'docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-01-native-docs-reader-design.md'
ANSI = re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]')


def need(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        sys.exit('pr-body.py: %s is missing; finish the step that writes it' % path)
    return path


def suite_line(path):
    t = ANSI.sub('', open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read())
    lines = [l.strip() for l in t.splitlines()]
    files = [l for l in lines if l.startswith('Test Files')]
    tests = [l for l in lines if re.match(r'^Tests\s', l)]
    if files or tests:
        return '%s; %s' % (files[-1] if files else 'no Test Files line', tests[-1] if tests else 'no Tests line')
    built = [l for l in lines if 'built in' in l]
    return built[-1] if built else 'no summary line: read the log'


def optional(name, default):
    p = os.path.join(S, name)
    return open(p, encoding='utf-8').read().strip() if os.path.exists(p) else default


head = subprocess.run(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
suites = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(S, 'w1-suite-*.log')))
if not suites:
    sys.exit('pr-body.py: no w1-suite-*.log in %s; run Steps 4 and 5 first' % S)
cite = open(need(os.path.join(S, 'w1-cite.txt')), encoding='utf-8').read().strip()
table = subprocess.run(['python3', os.path.join(S, 'mutate.py'), os.path.join(S, 'w1-rows.json'),
                        os.path.join(S, 'w1-mut'), 'report'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
r3 = json.load(open(need(os.path.join(S, 'r3-result.json')), encoding='utf-8'))

out = []
out.append('Wave 1 of the native Docs reader: **ccd reads docs**. Nothing calls these verbs yet; the grants, the '
           'adapter and the routes are W2 and W3.')
out.append('')
out.append('- Spec: %s%s' % (BLOB, SPEC))
out.append('- Plan: %s%s' % (BLOB, PLAN))
out.append('- Both links resolve once this PR merges; until then, read the spec and the plan in this PR\'s Files tab.')
out.append('- Measured at `%s`.' % head[:12])
out.append('')
out.append('## What ships')
out.append('')
out.append('- `shared/docs.ts` (L0, imports nothing): sections, caps, value grammars, the failure vocabulary and '
           'its retry classes, the one redactor, the ccd wire types, content classes and the raster table, the '
           'response headers, `resolveDocRef`, `admitDraft`/`entryView`, `githubBlobUrl`, the page grammar and '
           '`docsApi`.')
out.append('- `ccd/ccd`: `docs-index`, `docs-tree`, `docs-show` and `docs-fetch` at their final arity, one '
           'embedded python helper (`_docs_py`, python 3.8 floor, probed by the bash front), the five caps lines '
           'with `docs-v1`, the four dispatcher arms and the usage string. Restamped.')
out.append('- `ccd/ccrc-doctor-checks`: the `docs` check (counts only, never a project name) and the python3 '
           'reason.')
out.append('- No `server/src`, `agent/src` or `pwa/src` change, no `FLEET_PROTO` bump, and `EXEC_COMMANDS` is '
           'still `[\'tmux\',\'ccd\']`.')
out.append('')
out.append('## Deploy class')
out.append('')
out.append('Fleet box only (ccd and the doctor checks). No rollout by hand: the boxes follow the dev channel. '
           'Once the fleet box runs this build, its `ccrc doctor` `docs` line is the first proof on a real box.')
out.append('')
out.append('## Suites (foreground, this branch)')
out.append('')
out.append('| Run | Result |')
out.append('|---|---|')
for p in suites:
    name = os.path.basename(p)[len('w1-suite-'):-len('.log')]
    out.append('| %s | %s |' % (name, suite_line(p).replace('|', '\\|')))
out.append('')
out.append('## Citation census (S6-R11)')
out.append('')
out.append('```')
out.append(cite)
out.append('```')
out.append('')
out.append('## Mutation table')
out.append('')
out.append('Every row was applied alone to a `git archive` copy of this branch (never the worktree), its test files '
           'run with `--bail=1`, and the file restored byte for byte. The unmutated copy was green before the '
           'first row and again after the last. `R4b` is the spec\'s own row-4 mutation (drop `--full-tree`), '
           'red through the literal ls-tree argv that Task 10 pins.')
out.append('')
out.append(table)
out.append('')
notes = optional('w1-table-notes.md', '')
if notes:
    out.append('Notes on the table:')
    out.append('')
    out.append(notes)
    out.append('')
out.append('## R3 (lab)')
out.append('')
out.append('A `git clone --shared` of the fleet project with the most worktrees, in a fixture HOME, with as many '
           'worktree records as the live checkout counts (%d) and %d dirty docs in one holder (%d of them '
           'tracked docs modified). The project is not named here.' % (r3['records'], r3['dirty'],
                                                                         r3['modifiedTracked']))
out.append('')
out.append('| Measure | Value | Bound |')
out.append('|---|---|---|')
out.append('| first run | %d ms | 8000 ms |' % r3['coldMs'])
out.append('| warm p95 (10 runs, nearest rank) | %d ms | 2000 ms |' % r3['warmP95Ms'])
out.append('| warm runs | %s | |' % ', '.join('%d' % x for x in r3['warmMs']))
out.append('| entries listed | %d | |' % r3['entries'])
out.append('')
out.append('Verdict: **%s**.%s' % ('pass' if r3['pass'] else 'over the bound',
                                   '' if r3['pass'] else ' Per spec 7.8, the read-lane wait is re-derived from these '
                                   'numbers before W3 merges.'))
out.append('')
out.append('With status sleeping past a lowered per-call bound, the draft phase answered `%s`, and the committed '
           'listing survived with %d entries.' % (json.dumps(r3['degraded'], sort_keys=True), r3['listingSurvived']))
out.append('')
out.append('## Deviations')
out.append('')
out.append(optional('w1-deviations.md', 'None. This wave minted no deviation number.'))
out.append('')
out.append('## For review')
out.append('')
out.append('- `test-macos` and `probe-macos` are advisory and flaky by ruling; they gate nothing.')
out.append('- Merging is the coordinator\'s, after the review run rules, with `gh pr merge --admin` (the repo\'s '
           'ruleset wants an approval nobody can give).')
review = optional('w1-review-notes.md', '')
if review:
    out.append(review)
out.append('')
out.append('\U0001F916 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)')
print('\n'.join(out))
````
